topics.topic: Scope and precedence of A01 depth validation relative to operation-schema validation
questions: Does A01’s newly inserted “depth” mean only the request message’s depth, or must every carried JSON text also pass its depth check before operation-schema validation?
When a request both fails its operation schema and contains an over-depth JSON text in a string field, which failure takes precedence?

quotes: answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; the depth check of the request message below, else invalid_request; for tools/call, the message names a catalogue operation, fits that operation's request model with no unknown field and has every JSON text it carries made canonical by the replacement below — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null; the fit is pydantic's in JSON mode, the request model's model_validate_json over the canonical JSON text of the arguments with strict=True, since strict validation of Python objects refuses an enum given as its value string and a tuple given as a JSON array, which is how every request carries them; a ValueError the fit raises (pydantic's ValidationError is one) is raised again as InvalidRequestError, so translate_failure answers invalid_request, never internal_error — and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1). initialize, ping and tools/list name no catalogue operation and are answered after the depth check, as the note on methods says.

answer_request: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] As part of the fit check, before the actor check and before any handler runs, MUST replace every JSON text the request carries — the json_text of each RequestJsonValue and RequestConstant, the value_schema of every Port and RequestConstant, the guard_value of every EdgeGuard — by its canonical form obtained from canonical_bytes; a NonCanonicalValueError there is invalid_request, so modules below receive only canonical JSON (A01 rule 1).
judgement.why: The later surface notes distinguish the outer message-depth check from carried-text canonicalization and place operation-model fitting before canonicalizing carried JSON texts, so an operation-schema failure takes precedence.
